clips.title: 50亿投入：换不来盈利，金主为何提前撤资

subtitles.en: Now we do want to get back to that breaking news in the world of sports that just crossed the Bloomberg terminal disinvolving live golf bankruptcy filing in the state of New Jersey
subtitles.zh: 现在我们要回到体育界的突发新闻，刚刚在彭博终端上出现的关于LIV高尔夫在新泽西州申请破产保护的消息。

subtitles.en: joining us right now to talk a little bit more about this is Bloomberg senior sports reporter Randall Williams.
subtitles.zh: 现在加入我们的是彭博社资深体育记者兰德尔·威廉姆斯。

subtitles.en: Not a surprise, I assume. Yeah. No, not at all.
subtitles.zh: 我猜这并不意外。是的，一点也不意外。

subtitles.en: I mean, you look at all the money that live as laws versus the money that they've made and there is an astronomical difference to when the Saudis are funding this and when they weren't.
subtitles.zh: 看看LIV的投入和收入，差距巨大，尤其是在沙特资金支持与否的情况下。

subtitles.en: Yeah. So this isn't a surprise at all. So, yeah.
subtitles.zh: 所以这完全不意外。是的。

subtitles.en: And that's kind of the key phrase here. It doesn't seem like they're really funding as they're providing a little bit of a bridge here for the bankruptcy process.
subtitles.zh: 这里的关键是，他们似乎并没有真正提供资金，只是为破产程序提供了一点过渡性支持。

subtitles.en: But do you have any sense as to why they couldn't have found a way to sort of make this work?
subtitles.zh: 但你知道为什么他们没能找到办法让这件事成功吗？

subtitles.en: I mean, what was sort of the real tripping point? I think the optics are is that the Saudis were pushing live golf and with a $5 billion
subtitles.zh: 真正的转折点是什么？我认为表面上看，沙特在推动LIV高尔夫，投入了50亿美元。

subtitles.en: rocket ship. And when you pull the plug on that and say, okay, we haven't made money enough, of course they pulled the plug a lot earlier than live golf executives anticipated.
subtitles.zh: 当资金被切断，他们说我们没赚到足够的钱，当然他们切断资金的时间比LIV高管预期的要早得多。

subtitles.en: But at that point, if you're going out there to the market and saying, we have not been able to turn over a profit and yet $5 billion had been invested in you, then it's going to raise a lot of questions from people who you have conversations with.
subtitles.zh: 但那时，如果你对市场说我们未能盈利，而你已经投入了50亿美元，那就会引起与你对话的人的许多疑问。

subtitles.en: I remember when this started, there was a lot of head scratching, but then you saw the talent that they got.
subtitles.zh: 我记得刚开始时，大家都很困惑，但后来看到他们签下的球员。

subtitles.en: You know, they spent a lot for that talent. Of course. But they got some big talent there.
subtitles.zh: 他们为这些球员花了很多钱，当然，但确实签下了一些大牌。

subtitles.en: And, you know, it was a little bit of a looser game, the crowd was a little more fun.
subtitles.zh: 而且比赛氛围更轻松，观众也更有趣。

subtitles.en: And, you know, for those of us, I mean, I'm a big golfer and, you know, I don't like the state nature of golf.
subtitles.zh: 对我们这些高尔夫爱好者来说，我不喜欢高尔夫的传统严肃。

subtitles.en: I even thought I was going to club this weekend and it was very like, you know, dress code and everything.
subtitles.zh: 我甚至以为这周末要去俱乐部，那里有严格的着装要求。

subtitles.en: Yeah, I was very excited. It was fine.
subtitles.zh: 是的，我很兴奋，感觉不错。

winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架

让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
